keys.meta_title: CPS Test: Free Click Speed Test with Real Tapping Norms | CoreSkillAI
keys.meta_desc: Free click speed test. Click for 5, 10 or 30 seconds and get your clicks per second, steadiest rate and best second, compared with 1,519 adults in a published tapping study.
keys.cps_desc: How many times can you click in 10 seconds? Get your clicks per second, compared with a published finger tapping study.
keys.cps_how1: Choose 5, 10 or 30 seconds, and the mouse (or touch screen) or the spacebar.
keys.cps_how2: The clock starts with your first click. Click as fast as you can until the time is up.
keys.cps_how3: For a fair comparison, use one finger of the hand you normally click with and rest your palm, as in the clinical tapping test.
keys.cps_how4: You get your clicks per second, your steadiest rate, your best single second and how even your rhythm was.
keys.cps_start_desc: Measures how many times you can click in a set time, using the same idea as the finger tapping test used in neuropsychology.
keys.cps_done: Time is up. Your results are below.
keys.cps_note_few: Too few clicks to score. Click as fast as you can for the whole time.
keys.cps_note_auto: Your intervals were almost perfectly even, which a human hand does not produce. If an auto-clicker was used, this is not a measurement.
keys.cps_note_tech: That is faster than one-finger tapping reached in the reference study, so you probably used another technique, such as jitter or butterfly clicking. The percentile assumes one finger.
keys.cps_note_5s: A 5-second run is too short to compare with the reference study. Choose 10 or 30 seconds for a percentile.
keys.cps_note_space: The reference study used a mouse button, so a spacebar comparison is only approximate.
keys.cps_pct: Faster than about {p}% of adults in the reference study.
keys.cps_disclaimer: Click speed depends on your mouse or screen, your technique and practice. It measures motor speed, not intelligence or health.
